pl-echinodorus-horizontalis.title: Brazilian Sword (emersed)
pl-echinodorus-horizontalis.summary: Brazilian Sword (emersed) is a roots-in-water / pond-margin plant with slow growth (easy care).
rows: Roots-in-water (emersed / pond margin; not a fully submerged aquarium plant)
Pond margin / emersed planter (roots in water)
Heavy. Grown with roots in water or damp soil; not an underwater carpet plant
Root and water feeding. Nutrient-rich water or soil helps
Divide the rhizome into pieces with a few leaves or fronds each
notes: Keep roots wet; leaves prefer air. Not a fully submerged aquarium plant.
Fewer independent public profiles exist for this cultivar; fields stick to what the available source states.
warn: Not for fully submerged long-term use unless the species is known to adapt underwater.

pl-dracaena-sanderiana.title: Lucky Bamboo
pl-dracaena-sanderiana.sci: Dracaena sanderiana (also sold as D. braunii)
pl-dracaena-sanderiana.summary: Not a true bamboo — a West African Dracaena sold as curly or straight “lucky bamboo.” Keep roots and the lower stem in water and all leaves above the surface; fully submerged foliage rots.
rows: Upright segmented stems with lance-shaped leaves (straight or trained curly forms)
Open-top aquarium rim, paludarium, or vase with roots in water
Bright indirect light; avoid harsh direct sun that scorches leaves
Often 30–100+ cm (1–3+ ft) in trade cuts; can reach about 1.2 m (4 ft) over time
Moderate. Fibrous roots that anchor in pebbles, gravel, or a shallow pot; keep the crown above deep substrate
Water-column / dilute liquid feed when grown in water; weak fertilizer sparingly. In substrate, light root feeding helps
Room temperature about 65–90°F (18–32°C); typical home/aquarium room temps are fine
Not critical in water culture; use dechlorinated water
Soft to hard tap is usually fine; avoid chronically stagnant water
Stem cuttings at nodes; root in water
notes: Curly and straight lucky bamboo and “Dracaena sanderiana” listings are the same species.
Change vase or display water regularly so stems do not sit in foul, stagnant water.
warn: Do not bury the whole plant underwater — submerged leaves and stems rot and foul the tank.

pl-houttuynia-cordata-chameleon.title: Chameleon Plant (Houttuynia)
pl-houttuynia-cordata-chameleon.sci: Houttuynia cordata 'Chameleon' (syn. 'Variegata' / 'Tricolor'; catalog: H. cordata varigata)
pl-houttuynia-cordata-chameleon.summary: A colorful, heart-leaved bog plant with green, cream, pink and red variegation. Best as a roots-in-water or pond-margin plant in a pot — it spreads aggressively by rhizomes if planted loose.
rows: Roots-in-water / marginal bog plant (leaves usually emersed; tolerates shallow water over the crown)
Spreading rhizomatous perennial with heart-shaped variegated leaves
Open-top aquarium margin, paludarium, or contained pond basket
Bright light to partial shade; strongest leaf color in brighter light
Aggressive spreader. Long rhizomes; keep in a pot or barrier or it will colonize wet areas
Root feeder in moist soil or aquatic planting media; also takes nutrients from wet margins
About 60–75°F (15–24°C) indoors; hardy outdoors in much of the temperate zone when used in ponds
Easy to grow; hard to contain
East and Southeast Asia (species); ‘Chameleon’ is a garden cultivar
notes: Catalog spelling “varigata” matches the trade variegated/Chameleon form.
Bruised leaves are aromatic; plant is invasive in garden soils — use a rigid pot.
warn: Aggressive rhizome spreader — do not plant loose in open beds or uncontained pond edges.

sources.name: Ohio State Pocket Gardener – Houttuynia cordata ‘Chameleon’

pl-syngonium-podophyllum.title: Arrowhead Vine
pl-syngonium-podophyllum.summary: A common houseplant with arrow-shaped juvenile leaves, sold for roots-in-water use on open aquariums. Keep foliage above water; roots in the tank help take up nutrients.
rows: Roots-in-water (emersed leaves; only roots/stem bases in water)
Vining aroid; juvenile leaves arrow-shaped, mature leaves more divided
Hang on the rim or place in a cup/filter outflow so leaves stay dry
Moderate to fast in good light
Vines can trail or climb several feet over time; trim to size
Moderate. Water roots form readily along stems in hydroponic/aquarium water culture
Water-column feeder when rooted in aquarium water; dilute houseplant fertilizer if grown in a vase alone
Stem cuttings that root in water
notes: Catalog lists “Arrowhead” in Roots-in-Water Plants with no scientific name; in that category the trade plant is Syngonium podophyllum (arrowhead vine), not Sagittaria.
warn: Toxic if chewed (calcium oxalate) — keep leaves away from pets and children who might nibble.
